C runs every resolved command as d->character, which for a switched descriptor is the mobile (its send_to_char/act TO_CHAR reach the player). The matrix runs the descriptorless-NPC lanes (say/tell/emote/shout/gossip/auction/wake/follow/group/report/give/stand/sit/rest/sleep/ride/dismount) with a valid and an invalid argument as a switched mobile; a lane that answers CharacterCommandUnsupported falls through to the session handler instead of silently doing nothing.

Follow-up to the switched-body command matrix: C's do_hit sets WAIT_STATE(PULSE_VIOLENCE+2) on the switched mobile (src/act.offensive.c:126), so with hit/murder/kill issued back to back the next command stays queued and its block is empty; Go runs it immediately and prints the refusal. First divergent block: switched-body-command-matrix-depth "hit Nobody" after a real hit — C empty, Go "They don't seem to be here." The silent-swallow the matrix fixes is addressed (Go prints); this is the wait-state arm, not the lane's output.

do_simple_move renders the room when the mover has a descriptor (src/act.movement.c:266-269). A switched mobile that flees successfully has a descriptor, so C renders the destination room to it; Go's doSimpleMoveMob calls entry_prog instead, so a switched flee emits only "You flee head over heels." First divergent block: switched-body-command-matrix-depth "flee" — C destination room look, Go only the flee line (the matrix ships without the combat/flee lines).
A switched low-level mobile misses the immortal command row in the search and answers Huh?!?, because the ladder searches with the body's own level (R1/R2/R5e/R5g/R5h).
